space-needle.name: Space Needle & Seattle Center
space-needle.blurb: The 605-ft (184 m) 1962 World's Fair tower with its flying-saucer top, glass "Loupe" floor and the Seattle Center grounds at its feet.

spawn.note: South base plaza by the Howard S. Wright fountain looking north up at the Needle.

extent.description: Needle base pavilion and plaza, Howard S. Wright Memorial Fountain, Chihuly exterior, Monorail station and track, MoPOP south front, Broad St / 5th Ave N edges.
extent.edges: Broad St (south-west), 5th Ave N (east, monorail columns), Thomas St (north). Fences of Chihuly garden and Needle ticketed areas.

structures.name: Space Needle (1962; John Graham Jr. / Edward Carlson; Victor Steinbrueck)

dims.osm_parts: core/legs to 152.4 m; saucer glass bands 152.4–156.1 and 158.1–161.2 m; roof 166.9–170.3 m; pyramidal spire cap to 181.1 m; SkyLine ring 30.5–36.6 m; mid ring 61.0–64.0 m

structures.form: Three pairs of slender tapering steel legs (6 columns) forming an hourglass "waist" around a central core with three exterior glass elevators (41 s ride), a ring at 100 ft (SkyLine banquet level), and the top-house: disc ("halo") with sloping glass observation deck at 520 ft, The Loupe revolving glass floor below (2018), roof cone and ~mast/beacon at the top.
structures.paint_history: 1962: Orbital Olive body, Astronaut White legs, Re-entry Red saucer, Galaxy Gold roof; Galaxy Gold roof again 2012 and 2022–2023.
structures.night: Floodlit white from the base, lit ring under the saucer; 85-million-candela "Legacy Light" beam shines skyward on holidays; NYE fireworks off the tower.

plaques.title: 605 feet
plaques.text: Built for the 1962 World's Fair, the Space Needle is 605 ft (184 m) tall and was the tallest structure west of the Mississippi when it opened.

plaques.title: Built fast
plaques.text: It was finished in less than a year; the last elevator car was installed the day before the fair opened on April 21, 1962.

plaques.title: Original colours
plaques.text: 1962 paint: Orbital Olive, Astronaut White, Re-entry Red and Galaxy Gold — the gold roof returned for the 50th and 60th anniversaries.

plaques.title: Glass floor
plaques.text: Since 2018 "The Loupe" has a revolving glass floor that turns once every 45 minutes.

plaques.title: Built to last
plaques.text: The tower is designed for 200 mph winds and a magnitude 9.0 earthquake; its foundation weighs as much as the tower above ground.

interaction.primary: Ride the elevator (41 s cut-scene) to the observation deck: a 360° view from 158 m using a pre-rendered or low-poly city panorama + the Loupe glass floor (look down).
secondary: Lie on the lawn and look up (camera preset)
Catch the monorail (fast-travel to Westlake / Pike Place spot)

iconic.frame: Straight up the legs from the south base

alternates.name: Needle + Glasshouse
alternates.frame: Chihuly Glasshouse in front of the Needle

seasonal: Summer: Bumbershoot / Folklife festivals on the grounds (Labor Day, Memorial Day)
Winter: Winterfest; low sun lights the saucer orange at sunset (~16:20)

structures.name: MoPOP (2000, Frank O. Gehry)

dims.height_m: ≈ 26–30 m at highest lobes (estimate; OSM Sky Church part 22 m)

structures.form: Several bulging, folded blob volumes clad in shingles, each mass a different colour/finish, with a crumpled "guitar neck" steel ribbon sculpture rising on top; the Monorail runs through a slot in the building; glass entrance; Sky Church hall inside (large LED screen).

colours.note: Panels are rectangular shingles in a staggered grid with visible fastener dots; the iridescent ("chameleon") mass shifts gold→orange→magenta→purple with view angle (use thin-film / angle-based colour ramp), blue and silver masses are matte-satin, the canopy over the monorail is mirror stainless. dialogueGeneral.usage: Pedestrian set for the Seattle and Bellevue driving districts and as filler in every spot. ctx: greeting|bumped|photographed|idle|spot|rain|honked_at|near_miss; non-English lines carry orig+lang with English text.

tone.note: "Seattle Freeze": locals are described as "very polite but not particularly friendly" to strangers — keep local NPC lines courteous, brief, low-key; few unprompted chats.
Washington ranked 48th of 50 states for extraversion (2008 study cited by Wikipedia) — locals default to nods, "sorry", "you're good".

Honking is rare and seen as rude: ~3 in 4 Northwest drivers said they rarely or never honk (PEMCO 2017); attitudes softened by 2021 (65% say honking at least somewhat appropriate). NPC reaction to player honking near spots: surprised/disapproving, not aggressive.
Coffee culture: Seattle drinks more coffee than any other US city; espresso small talk is a safe icebreaker.
Rain talk is universal small talk; locals rarely use umbrellas (hoods/rain shells) — common local self-image, unsourced folklore: keep light.

Visitors: Canada was 73% of Seattle's 2.4 M international visitors in 2024; then China, India, UK, South Korea, Germany, Japan, Australia, France, Taiwan — languages used: English, French (Québec), Mandarin, Hindi, Korean, German, Japanese, Spanish (domestic + Latin America).
Indigenous art (totems, Salish Welcome): staff/guides speak respectfully; no jokes about sacred objects.
Guardrails: no stereotypes, accents written phonetically, slurs, politics or alcohol jokes about any group; tourists are curious and happy, locals helpful-but-reserved.
